subject: DPA redlines: subprocessor list & telemetry data use (WellCare AI)
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@wellcare.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Legal Intake <legal@wellcare.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 12:04:00 -0400
Subject: WellCare DPA redlines (v2) - subprocessors, telemetry

Kimberly / team,

Thanks for the call today. Attach is our updated DPA with a few redlines: we want an explicit, flat list of subprocessors (we can't accept an open-ended allowlist), an unequivocal prohibition on using customer data for model training, and a clause that requires 30-day notice before any new telemetry export.

Can you confirm which of these are deal-breakers and what evidence you can provide for SOC2 type controls and data residency? We need to get this on our procurement track this week (contracting deadline 2028-04-22).

Attachments: WellCare_DPA_redline_v2.pdf, subprocessors_proposed_list.xlsx, telemetry_clause_diff.txt

Regards,
Tom Ellis
Head of Legal Operations
WellCare AI

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@wellcare.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: WellCare DPA redlines (v2) - subprocessors, telemetry

Team — looping you both in.

Quick context: WellCare pushed three big asks (flat subprocessors list, no-training clause, 30-day notice for telemetry exports). They flagged procurement deadline 4/22. They copied legal intake. I told Tom we'd do a product + security feasibility check and come back with a single position this week.

Avery: can product confirm whether a flat subprocessor list is operationally feasible (we have dynamic infra partners). Also want a short note on what telemetry we collect and whether exports can be constrained per customer.
Olga: can security confirm evidence bundle (SOC2, encryption in transit/rest, KMS) and stance on no-training prohibition?

We should aim to provide a counterproposal by EOD Wednesday (4/17). If any of these are deal-breakers, call it out.

Thanks — Kimberly
Senior Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@wellcare.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: WellCare DPA redlines (v2) - subprocessors, telemetry

Kimberly / Olga / Marcus — thanks for the ping. High-level product notes below; flagging where I need input from security and ops.

1) Flat subprocessor list: operationally we rely on a few dynamic infra partners (cloud provider regions, specialized inference hosts, metrics vendor). Providing a single static list is risky because we may add/replace infra partners over time for scalability/availability. We can:
  - Offer a committed list of current subprocessors (we can attach the current inventory) + a 30-day notice for additions, with an exception process for security-critical patches (shorter notice but documented).
  - Alternatively, agree to a shortlist of classes (e.g., "cloud compute providers, metrics and observability vendors, managed MLOps partners") plus a requirement we notify changes.

2) No-training clause: product position — we already have an explicit no-training commitment for customer-provided prompt/PK data in the standard agreement for this product tier. The ask forms as an absolute ban on any downstream model improvement using any derived signals (including aggregate telemetry). That would materially limit our ability to ship model improvements and to use aggregated performance telemetry to tune latency/cost heuristics.
  - Mitigation option: commit to "no use of customer-identifiable data for model training" and allow strictly aggregated, differentially-processed telemetry for platform optimization. We can agree to retain telemetry at an aggregate/hashed level and provide a description of aggregation windows and retention.

3) 30-day notice for telemetry export: product question — what export scope do they mean (raw token payloads, KV cache snapshots, runtime metrics)? We can limit exports to anonymized metrics and redact payloads. For raw output exports, we need a business justification and an ops playbook.

Pending items I need from Olga/Marcus:
- Security: confirm what evidence we can share (SOC2 report redacted, encryption attestations, KMS/HSM attestations), and whether security can accept the suggested telemetry aggregation approach.
- Ops/Legal (Marcus): can we provide the current subprocessor inventory as an attachment and is there precedent for a 30-day notification with emergency patches carveout?

I will draft a short customer-facing counterproposal once we have security signoff.

— Avery
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@wellcare.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 13:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: WellCare DPA redlines (v2) - subprocessors, telemetry

Avery / all — security stance below. Short version: we can meet them on most items with constraints; the flat, immutable subprocessor list is the main blocker.

Evidence bundle we can provide (redactable copies): SOC 2 Type II summary (audit firm redactions), encryption-in-transit and at-rest attestations, KMS integration notes, recent pen-test high-level summary, and our subprocessors inventory (current). We can't share raw SOC2 reports unredacted.

Subprocessors: we will not accept a contractual requirement to maintain a permanently fixed list. Operational reality: we may add cloud partners for capacity/failover. Proposed counter: provide current inventory + commit to 30-day notice for additions; emergency additions allowed with post-facto notice and documented justification. Add a clause requiring Redwood to use commercially reasonable efforts to provide notice. This aligns with other enterprise deals.

No-training clause: we already enforce a "no training on customer identifiable data" policy at the service level for this tier. However, the customer's language is broader (disallowing use of aggregated telemetry). We can accept a prohibition on training on customer-identifiable or customer-labeled data, and allow aggregate/anonymous telemetry for platform optimization. To be conservative, we should add an implementation appendix describing what "aggregate" means (e.g., min sample sizes, hashing, no retention of raw payloads beyond operational windows). I'll draft suggested language.

Telemetry exports: acceptable if limited to metrics and scrubbed artifacts. Exports that include UTI or raw prompt/response data must be evaluated separately.

Action items for internal:
 - Marcus: prepare the current subprocessors inventory attachment and confirm whether Ops agrees to 30-day notice + emergency exception.
 - Avery: incorporate the product-lifecycle impact language (what we can vs can't promise) into the customer counterproposal.
 - Kimberly: plan for a short customer call if they push back on our counter.

I'll draft the recommended security clauses and send a redline v2b by EOD.

— Olga
Head of Product Security, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@wellcare.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Apr 2028 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: WellCare DPA redlines (v2) - subprocessors, telemetry

All — finalizing internal position and next steps.

Proposed customer-facing counter (short):
1) Subprocessors: attach current inventory (see attached spreadsheet). Redwood will provide 30 days' notice for additions; emergency additions allowed with documented justification and post-notification. We will not warrant a permanently fixed list.
2) No-training: Redwood confirms no training on customer-identifiable data. Platform optimization using aggregated, non-reversible telemetry is permitted; see appendix that defines aggregation thresholds and retention.
3) Telemetry exports: Redwood will provide exports limited to anonymized metrics on a 30-day notice; raw prompt/response exports require explicit SOW and scoping.

We can ship the evidence bundle (SOC2 summary, encryption notes) with redactions. Olga will circulate the security appendix and I will attach the current subprocessors spreadsheet.

Kimberly: recommend sending the counterproposal to Tom with an offer for a 30-minute alignment call Wednesday 4/18 morning (PST). If WellCare insists on a fixed subprocessor list or an absolute ban on aggregated telemetry, we escalate to VP Sales/legal.

I'll prepare the two-pager and circulate for one final review by 17:30 today.

Marcus Lin
Enterprise Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: subprocessors_proposed_list.xlsx (internal inventory)
